clue.text: Number on watch?

parts.note: read as the figures printed round a watch face, each of which is a single numeral

explanation.surface: Someone asks what figure is showing on a wristwatch.
explanation.definitionFit: A digit is a single numeral, such as the figures marking the hours on a watch face.

clue.text: One with relatives in the Home Guard initially, is on the march

indicators.note: the word in tells us the first pieces sit inside the initials of the wartime force
the first letter of the word it picks from

parts.note: the initials of the Home Guard, Britain's wartime volunteer defence force, are H and G
one is the Roman numeral I
kin means relatives, family

explanation.surface: A Home Guard volunteer with family in the unit sets off marching.
explanation.walkthrough: The Home Guard was Britain's Second World War force of part-time volunteers; 'initially' tells us to use its initials HG, which then hold I and KIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Hikers walk long distances on foot, so someone hiking is out walking, on the march.

clue.text: Unlucky place for William as things turned out

indicators.note: things that turn out differently end up rearranged, so the letters are reshuffled

explanation.surface: A remark that a certain spot proved ill-starred for a man named William, as events unfolded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned out' rearranges AS THINGS. The town on England's south coast is where William the Conqueror defeated Harold in 1066.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1066 battle in which William of Normandy won the English crown is named after this Sussex town.

clue.text: Supporters of persistent horses

definitions.meaning: stays are ropes or props that hold something up, so those that do so are supporters
racehorses with stamina for long distances

explanation.definitionFit: Stays are supports such as a mast's ropes; racing calls horses with stamina for long distances by the same name.

clue.text: Type of table only used in Autumn?

definitions.text: Type of table only used in Autumn?

parts.words: Type of table only used in Autumn?
parts.note: plays on the season when trees shed foliage, while describing a table with hinged flaps

explanation.surface: Someone asks about a piece of furniture brought out only in the fall season.
explanation.definitionFit: This table has hinged flaps that hang down when not in use, and in autumn leaves fall from trees.

clue.text: Angle for defence in Dyfed

parts.note: to angle is to fish with rod and line
a guard is a defence, something set up to protect

explanation.surface: An angler takes up a defensive position in a Welsh county.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Angle' is the verb to fish. Dyfed is a former county of south-west Wales; the port town is on its coast.
explanation.definitionFit: This ferry port on the Pembrokeshire coast lay within the old Welsh county of Dyfed.

clue.text: Self-appointed watchman leaving it in a bad way

indicators.note: something in a bad way is in disorder, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A self-appointed guard abandons his post in a sorry state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a bad way' rearranges the nine letters of LEAVING IT.
explanation.definitionFit: A vigilante takes on the job of policing a neighbourhood without any official authority.

clue.text: Railway assistance for a capital band

definitions.note: capital here means of the head, so a band worn on the head

parts.note: BR is British Rail, the old national railway
aid means assistance or help

explanation.surface: Rail aid is sent to support a band in a capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' is used in its sense of relating to the head, so the definition is a band for the hair, not a group from a capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: A plait of hair or a decorative ribbon trimming is a strip worn on or around the head.

clue.text: Bliss of oriental study

parts.note: oriental means eastern, abbreviated E
a den is a private room or study

explanation.surface: A scholar finds happiness in learning about the East.
explanation.definitionFit: The garden of Genesis stands for paradise, a state of perfect happiness.

clue.text: Service to make small cars go

parts.note: Minis are small British cars
a go is an attempt, a try

explanation.surface: A garage promises to get little motors running again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go' is a noun, an attempt; a Mini is a classic small British car.
explanation.definitionFit: A government department is a branch of public service; in church, the clergy's work is also ministry.

clue.text: Exercise in rude shed (innermost parts)

indicators.note: the word in tells us the exercise goes inside the reworked letters
rude here means crude, roughly made, so the letters of the shed are roughly rearranged

parts.note: PT is physical training, exercise

explanation.surface: A workout is held in a ramshackle garden shed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rude' is the anagram signal here, in its old sense of roughly made, not impolite; 'in' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The depths of something are its deepest, most central or remote reaches.

clue.text: The countryman's against a single drink

parts.note: a single thing is one, a
gin is a spirit, a drink

explanation.surface: A rustic objects to being served just one measure of spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition marks the word as rural dialect: country folk say it for 'against'.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a dialect form meaning opposed to, used in rustic speech.

clue.text: Fell-racer who never wins?

definitions.meaning: one who races up a fell, a hill in northern England
someone always finishing second, just behind the winner

explanation.walkthrough: A fell is a hill or moor in northern England, where fell-running races are held.
explanation.definitionFit: Read literally, it is someone running up a hill; as a set term, it is whoever comes second.

clue.text: Parisienne worker finds somewhere to eat on motorway

indicators.note: in a down clue, a piece written on another sits above it

parts.note: the M1 is Britain's first motorway, written MI
a dinette is a small dining area

explanation.surface: A Paris working girl finds a diner on a British motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 runs from London to Leeds; its name is taken as the letters MI.
explanation.definitionFit: In Paris, a young woman working as a shop assistant or seamstress was traditionally called this.

clue.text: Missouri area, perhaps, where we'd go astray in fog

indicators.note: the word in tells us the reworked letters sit inside the fog

parts.note: mist is a thin fog

indicators.note: letters that go astray wander out of place, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Travellers in the American heartland lose their way in thick weather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go astray' signals the anagram and 'in' the container; 'perhaps' marks Missouri as one example of the region.
explanation.definitionFit: Missouri is one of the states of the central northern United States region.

clue.text: But not the actor in the sole part

definitions.text: But not the actor in the sole part

parts.words: But not the actor in the sole part
parts.note: plays on a one-person role versus a tiny role whose holder merely crosses the stage, with sole hinting at feet

explanation.surface: A cast note says someone other than the star of a one-man show.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a performer with a tiny non-speaking role, merely moving across the stage, far from the lead.

clue.text: Georgia's passion can have several elements in it

definitions.text: can have several elements in it

parts.note: GA is the abbreviation of the US state of Georgia, and the 's adds an S
fire means passion, ardour

explanation.surface: A woman named Georgia has a passion that holds many parts.
explanation.walkthrough: The heater's glowing parts are called elements, which is the joke in the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A domestic heater burning gas has radiant parts called elements that glow red.

clue.text: Description of Wells, we hear, bursting into tears in front of Ian

indicators.note: in a down clue, a piece in front of another comes first, above it
tears that burst are broken up, so the letters are scattered

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An account of the writer Wells that has listeners weeping before a man called Ian.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bursting into' signals the anagram and 'in front of' the order. 'we hear' tells us Wells is the spoken word, holes for water, not the writer H. G. Wells.
explanation.definitionFit: Such wells tap water under natural pressure, so it rises without pumping.

clue.text: Summary to the point and spot on

parts.note: a precis is a summary
E, east, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: A summary that is concise and exactly right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'point' is a compass point, here E for east.
explanation.definitionFit: Exact and accurate in every detail, hitting the mark exactly.

clue.text: Fellow in Hamlet, say, who has a beer after 6.50?

indicators.note: after tells us the beer is written behind the Roman numerals

parts.note: in Roman numerals 6 is VI and 50 is L
lager is a kind of beer

explanation.surface: A character from Shakespeare's tragedy orders a pint just before seven.
explanation.walkthrough: Hamlet the play misleads; a hamlet is a small settlement, and one living there is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A hamlet is a tiny settlement, so a man living in one is a resident of a rural community.

clue.text: Gun-point opening

parts.note: gat is slang for a gun
E, east, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: A firearm is aimed at a gap.
explanation.definitionFit: A gateway is an entrance, a way through a fence or wall.

clue.text: Ship's biscuit for this change of course

definitions.meaning: hard biscuit eaten by sailors, as in hardtack
a sailing ship changes direction by turning into the wind

explanation.definitionFit: Hardtack was hard ship's bread; in sailing, a change of direction into the wind is the same word.

clue.text: Credit reduced-bad deal in the first place

parts.note: credit shortened to its abbreviation is CR

indicators.note: a bad deal is a messed-up one, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Credit is cut after a poor bargain in the first instance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reduced' shortens Credit to CR; 'bad' rearranges DEAL to ADLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A baby's bed is the origin of a life, so the word stands for a birthplace or source.

clue.text: Was it changed by diet?

indicators.note: the words are changed in form, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A slimmer wonders whether dieting has made a difference.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changed' rearranges WAS IT, and the whole clue describes the body part a slimmer hopes to shrink.
explanation.definitionFit: Dieting is meant to reduce the middle of the body, the part a belt goes round.

clue.text: Bond agent

definitions.meaning: to bond is to stick together firmly
a substance that binds materials together

explanation.definitionFit: The building material binds bricks together, and a binding substance is a bonding agent.

clue.text: eg. Selkirk players on opponents' ground

parts.note: the cast are the players in a show
a team playing away is on the other side's ground

explanation.surface: A Scottish town's team is playing at its rivals' ground.
explanation.walkthrough: Selkirk is also a Scottish town, but here it is Alexander Selkirk, the marooned sailor who inspired Robinson Crusoe.
explanation.definitionFit: Alexander Selkirk was marooned on a Pacific island for four years, a shipwreck survivor stranded alone.

clue.text: Condescend to Kate Hardcastle's attitude

definitions.meaning: to condescend is to lower oneself
the heroine of Goldsmith's comedy She ... to Conquer, who poses as a barmaid

explanation.definitionFit: To lower oneself is to condescend; Kate Hardcastle's bending low is the title of Goldsmith's comedy.

clue.text: Start his tables turning

indicators.note: tables turning are overturned, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone starts flipping over the furniture.
explanation.definitionFit: To establish something is to found or set it up from the beginning.
